messages:
maya: Heads-up — running a dry-run of the 02:00 UTC change window now. This touches API, runtime, console, and router. Objective: validate the traffic quarantine + version-bridge behavior and ensure rollback keys are working. @kevin @sasha please ack if you have any staging pins or running canaries.
kevin: Acked. No long-running pins on API but runtime has a staging pool pinned to v3.14 for perf tests. I'll unpin at T-15 if everything looks green.
sasha: Quick checklist: release notes uploaded here: https://go/release/174820; migration command is recorded, KV migration is a read-only toggle for this dry-run so no schema changes.
sasha: Also, console has a header-swap feature flag that needs to be toggled to allow the router to route to the version-bridge. I'll flip in staging now and revert after the run.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary wave 1 started: id=cb-174820-1 services=[api,runtime,console,router] footprint=staging. Monitoring: latency, error-rate, 5xx. Canary TTL=10m.
ryan: Noted — I'll watch telemetry dashboards. If error-rate > 1% for 3 consecutive mins, we should abort and fall back to pinned variant.
kevin: Question — runtime's kv-eviction tunable is still on the new kernel path. If we see kv thrash, do we rollback runtime alone or hold on router? Preference: single-service rollback for faster recovery.
maya: Good question. Our fallback policy for this window is: 1) if runtime-specific regressions, rollback runtime to last pinned variant; 2) if cross-service contract break (headers/schema mismatch) then hold traffic and rollback router/console together. I'll update release notes with that explicit criteria.
sasha: Adding the exact rollback command snippets for quick copy/paste:
```
# rollback runtime to pinned variant
deployctl rollout abort --service runtime --to-version pinned
# hold router traffic to stable lane
deployctl traffic hold --service router --reason "quarantine-fallback"
```
kevin: Thanks. Also, are we using the version-bridge (shim) for model-serving routing? If so, confirm that API accepts both old/new header shapes during the transition.
maya: Yes, version-bridge enabled in staging. API accepts both shapes for 20m grace. Console will send the new header after header-swap feature flag flips.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary metrics update: wave 1: latency +2%, errors 0.1%, kv-miss rate stable. No automated abort. Next wave scheduled in 5m.
ryan: Seeing a small uptick in evictions on runtime nodes (0.8 -> 1.6 per sec). Not critical yet but keep an eye.
kevin: I'll throttle batch size on runtime canary (reduce max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 1024) and push config to the canary pool.
sasha: Pushed flag: console.header_swap=true for staging. Confirmed route mapping intact.
maya: Update: performing the simulated rollback drill for runtime to verify command flow. Will not actually roll unless we hit the thresholds.
kevin: Drill successful — rollback command executed in dry-run mode, no impact.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary wave 2 started: id=cb-174820-2.
ryan: Wave 2 telemetry looks clean. Evictions trending down after throttle.
maya: Ok — plan: let the canaries finish their TTL, then we run a quick smoke on production-like traffic in staging. If all green, we schedule the real change window. If anything breaches the thresholds documented above, we follow the single-service rollback path first.
sasha: I'll pre-write the release note blurb including the rollback instructions and the post-mortem checklist items, then share the link.
kevin: One last ask — add the exact runbook pointer to the console for oncall (just in case).
maya: Will do. Thank you all. Will post final signoff 30m before the real window. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary wave 1 and 2 completed. No abort. Dry-run complete. Logs: https://go/logs/canary/174820
